newsitem.title: USA: HP extends U.S. small business PC line.
newsitem.headline: HP extends U.S. small business PC line.

text.p: Hewlett-Packard Co said it will introduce on Monday new entry-level business models of its HP Vectra 500 Series PC in the U.S. and Canada markets, with street prices as low as $1,094.

With availability set for March 1, the entry level HP Vectra 520 5/133 Business desktop PC will have 16 megabytes of Random Access Memory (RAM), a 133 megahertz Intel Pentium Processor, a 256 kilobyte cache and a 1.2 gigabyte hard drive.

The HP Vectra 525MCx 5/200M Advanced Business Communication minitower PC has 32 megabytes of RAM, an Intel Pentium 200 Megahertz processor with MMX technology, a 256 kilobyte cache, a 3.8 gigabyte hard drive and a 16x Max CD-ROM Drive.

The higher-end machine also comes with a graphics card with two megabytes of video memory, a 33.6 kilobits per second data fax/voice modem and pre-installed Microsoft Word and Publisher software starting at $2,601, the company said.

Customers who buy PCs with the Microsoft Word and Publisher pre-installed can upgrade to Microsoft Office at a discounted rate, and an AT&T WorldNet Service icon has been added to all Advanced Communications Models for Internet access.
HP's Small Business Computing Operation, which markets the personal computer line, said the models also come with on-line help, a message centre and administration software.

Separately, HP said it was introducing a fast Internet pack which includes a 56 kilobits per second modem based on the US Robotics x2 technology, enabling customers to upgrade with a vacant ISA slot and a simple installation disk.

The HP fast Internet Pack will be available in April for street prices as low as $169, with a $30 discount available to customers who buy the pack and certain models of the HP Vectra 500 Series PC before May 30, 1997.
The pack includes a modem cable, DataSafe remote backup service and CompuServe Internet service provider software as well as HP remote technical support software.
